reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any complete real inner-product space, f:E→ℝ an everywhere Fréchet differentiable function, X:ℝ→E a curve, z∈E, and α,T∈ℝ with α≥0 and T≥0. Suppose f is α-strongly convex on all of E in the convention
f((1−λ)x+λy) ≤ (1−λ)f(x)+λf(y) − (α/2)λ(1−λ)‖y−x‖²
for every x,y∈E and λ∈[0,1]. Suppose z is a global minimizer: f(z)≤f(x) for every x∈E. Suppose X is continuous on the closed interval [0,T], and for every s∈[0,T) its right derivative at s exists and equals −∇f(X(s)), where ∇f is the Riesz representative of the derivative of f. Then for every t∈(0,T],
0 ≤ f(X(t))−f(z) ≤ B(t),
where B(t)=‖X(0)−z‖²/(2t) when α=0, and B(t)=[α/(2(exp(αt)−1))]‖X(0)−z‖² when α≠0 (hence α>0 under the hypotheses).
The differential equation is assumed at time 0 and at every time strictly below T, but not at T. The conclusion includes T when T>0 and excludes 0; for T=0 there are no conclusion times and the differential equation hypothesis has empty time domain. No finite-dimensionality, second differentiability, gradient Lipschitz continuity, or uniqueness of the minimizer is assumed.
objects: Arbitrary complete real inner-product space E; function f:E→ℝ; curve X:ℝ→E; global minimizer z∈E; real parameters α,T.
domains: f on all E; X defined on all ℝ; continuity on [0,T]; right differential equation on [0,T); estimate on (0,T].
quantifiers: Universally quantified over E and its normed additive group, real inner-product and completeness structures, f, X, z, α,T; all hypotheses imply the stated estimate for every t in (0,T].
assumptions: α≥0; T≥0; f everywhere Fréchet differentiable; α-strong convexity on E with α/2 convention; z global minimizer; X continuous on [0,T]; right derivative X at each s∈[0,T) equals −∇f(X(s)).
conclusion: Nonnegative function-value gap, bounded by squared initial distance divided by 2t if α=0, otherwise by α times squared initial distance divided by 2(exp(αt)−1).
scopes: Right derivative uses the full half-line [s,∞); continuity includes both endpoints; no differential equation required at terminal time.
constant_dependencies: The upper bound depends only on α, t, and ‖X(0)−z‖². T only restricts the admitted times.
